## Summary

This course has provided an introduction to using software containers for
reproducible research. We have learnt how Podman Desktop can be used to retrieve
and run container images from container registries, as well as build and publish
images from local Containerfiles.

Several key ideas were:

1. Containers provide reproducible computing environments for research
   software: portable, repeatable and distributed without installation
2. Podman works with container images built to the widely adopted Open
   Container Initiative (OCI) specification, also used by Docker
3. GitHub workflows allow container builds and publication to be automated
   alongside software testing
4. Container images should be well labelled, documented and rebuildable to 
   make software FAIR

If you have any comments, suggestions, fixes or other feedback on this course,
please raise an issue on the GitHub repository. Good luck if
you are continuing on to learn about Kubernetes!

## Clean-up

You will probably have several container images and containers left in Podman
Desktop from this course. You are welcome to keep using them. Otherwise, we
recommend removing them. A quick way to do this is:

1. In the *Containers* pane, press *Prune*, which removes all stopped
   containers.
2. In the *Images* pane, press *Prune* again, which removes images that are not
   used by a container.

If you use Podman Desktop for other work, check what will be removed first. You
can instead delete individual entries using the bin icon.

## Further resources

### Podman and related technology

- [Podman Desktop docs](https://podman-desktop.io/docs): documentation
  for everything in the application we have used, plus additional features
- [dockerdocs guides](https://docs.docker.com/guides/): language-specific
  containerisation and more advanced guides that can be followed using Podman
- [Reproducible Computational Environments Using Containers](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/docker-introduction/):
  introductory course using Podman CLI for reproducible research from the
  Carpentries community
- [The Cloud Native SIG](https://cloudnative-sig.ac.uk/): community for
  cloud-native technologies in digital research infrastructure 

### Container registries

- [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/): the largest public registry, a good
  place to find official base images
- [GitHub Container Registry](https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-container-registry)
  (`ghcr.io`): the registry we used and recommended for images accompanying code
  repositories
- [Quay.io](https://quay.io/): a public registry run by Red Hat, the main
  sponsor of Podman

### Automation and standards

- [Intermediate Research Software
  Development](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/python-intermediate-development/):
  course including testing, Github development and collaborative work from the
  Carpentries community
- [GitHub workflow docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/workflows):
  how workflows are defined and triggered, for building on what we covered
- [Open Container Initiative](https://opencontainers.org/): organisation from
  The Linux Foundation responsible for container image and runtime standards
- [Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/): Recommended version number
  specification for software
